full_judgment:
2. The short facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this civil petition for leave to appeal are that the present petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No.68 of 1997 in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal praying for setting aside the preliminary and final decree dated 31.03.1988 and 16.06.1997 respectively passed in Partition Suit No. 89 of 1984 of that court on the ground of non-service of summon. 

 3. The opposite party No. 7 contested in that miscellaneous case by filing written objection. The material case of this contesting opposite party was that the partition suit was originally filed in the year 1968 and it was then numbered as Title Suit No. 203 of 1968 and subsequently on transfer it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 89 of 1984. That summons of that suit was duly served upon all the defendants including the petitioner; that some of the defendants who were close relations of the petitioner, contested that suit; that the petitioner being a close relation of the contesting defendants was fully aware of that suit and the decree passed therein. The further case of this contesting opposite party was that another defendant, namely, the defendant No.13 of that partition suit also filed a Miscellaneous Case being No. 21 of 1990 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the decree passed in that partition suit and that miscellaneous case was ultimately dismissed on contest; that the present petitioner knowing about all these facts filed the present miscellaneous case on false pleas. 

 4. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence and facts and circumstances, dismissed the miscellaneous case filed by this petitioner. This petitioner then preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 63 of 2001 in the court of the District Judge, Barisal against that judgment of the trial court. The said appeal was ultimately heard by the learned Joint District Judge, Barisal who allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment and order of the trail court. The contesting opposite party No. 7 preferred Civil Revision No. 2707 of 2003 calling in question the said judgment and order of the appellate court below and obtained rule. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing, made that rule absolute setting aside the judgment and order of the appellate court below and restoring those of the trial court by the impugned judgment and order. 

 7. Mr. Probir Neogi has made submission to the effect that in this miscellaneous case the opposite party could not prove at all that the summons of the original partition suit was served upon this petitioner and in the circumstances the trial court has committed illegality in rejecting the miscellaneous case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by this petitioner and the High Court Division also has committed error in affirming this judgment and order of the trial court. 

 11. In a case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure the petitioner is to prove also that he has filed the case within the statutory period of limitation. In the present case the petitioner could not prove this fact; rather there are ample facts and circumstances on record which tell that the petitioner filed this case long after the statutory period of limitation from the date of his knowledge about the decree in question.
